body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf C_{\mathbb Q}\) be realized so that, for rational covariance enclosures of input length \(L\), every rank, repeated-eigenspace, and projector-product decision of \(\mathsf C\) is certified with \(p_{\mathrm{bit}}\le\operatorname{poly}(L,n,\log\kappa,\log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau))\), total Boolean running time polynomial in the same quantities, and total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\)? The construction must terminate on every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\) and preserve Theorem 1's graph and encoder guarantees.
body.justification: This is the genuinely unresolved bridge from exact-real statistical certification to an executable finite-precision theorem.
body.gap: Corollary 4.5 of Sobczyk's April 27, 2025 arXiv full version, version 2, gives a certified Hermitian-definite spectral-projector primitive, and Dey et al. give bit-growth templates, but neither source budgets composed forward error for an adaptive CRL transcript with projector-product zero tests.
body.consumer: Its resolution would make the certificate suitable for the official implementation with machine-checkable rounding guarantees rather than heuristic floating-point thresholds.

obligation.what_is_open: A complete Turing-model proof for certified invariant subspaces with repeated positive eigenvalues and for the adaptively composed projector-product norm intervals.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives give operator gaps and exact-real perturbation bounds, but they do not provide a verified rational spectral-projector routine with explicit intermediate bit growth. A generic appeal to stable eigensolvers would not prove polynomial Boolean complexity or the required outward-rounding budget.
obligation.attempted: Rational perturbation bounds close covariance inversion, primitive formation, Weyl rank decisions, and the required working precision for those pieces. Polynomial-filter and contour-resolvent routes were considered, but neither has a declared theorem or a complete coefficient and rounding analysis in the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result:
The covariance-to-primitive part admits the following certified partial result.  If rational matrix centers have entrywise rounding radius at most \(2^{-p}\) and all matrices being inverted have smallest eigenvalue at least \((2\kappa)^{-1}\), then their operator perturbation is at most \(n2^{-p}\), the inverse perturbation is at most \(4\kappa^2n2^{-p}\), and the three-factor formula for each primitive matrix has perturbation at most \(C n\kappa^4 2^{-p}\) for an absolute rational constant \(C\).  Weyl intervals incur the same operator error.  Consequently covariance inversion, primitive formation, and all rank decisions can be certified with arithmetic error at most \(e_{\star}/8\) using
\[
 p=O\!\left(L+\log n+\log\kappa+\log(1/e_{\star})\right),
\]
and polynomially many Boolean operations.  This does not yet certify the repeated-eigenspace projectors and their adaptively composed product norms with the remaining \(e_{\star}/8\) budget.
